title: Down the Potomac
subtitle: From the falls to Mount Vernon: a short walk through the river that shaped the capital region.
author: StoryMaps sample

blocks.html: The Potomac runs 405 miles from the Allegheny Mountains to the Chesapeake Bay. Its last stretch above tidewater drops sharply over the fall line, and nearly everything about the region's history follows from that drop.

The fall line

Scroll to follow the river downstream. The map on the right moves with the story.

slides.html:
Great Falls

The river falls 76 feet in under a mile, through the narrow Mather Gorge. Boats could not get past it, so cargo had to stop here.

Georgetown

A tobacco port grew up at the head of navigation, the farthest point upriver that seagoing ships could reach.

An image slide

A slide can show an image, video or embedded page instead of the map. The map comes back on the next slide.

The National Mall

Much of the Mall and West Potomac Park sits on land dredged from the river's tidal flats in the 1880s.

Old Town Alexandria

Downstream, Alexandria's deep-water port competed with Georgetown for the river trade.

The whole route

Zoomed out, the run from the falls to Mount Vernon is about 30 miles.

blocks.text: The river is the reason the city is where it is.
